item.title: Southington football scores 31 straight to beat Maloney and surge back atop CIAC Class LL playoff rankings
item.description: Head coach Rob Levesque talks to his Southington football team after their 38-14 CCC Tier 1 victory over Maloney at Falcon Field in Meriden on Friday night, Nov. 13, 2026. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) MERIDEN - Southington running back Ben Beaulieu sent his coach Rob Levesque a late-night text message this past week saying he'd also be available to play defense if needed for Friday night's CCC Tier 1 football showdown with Maloney. He didn't say anything about scoring touchdowns. Guess he didn't have to. That part was probably understood. Beaulieu scored three touchdowns, including two game-changers early in the fourth quarter, to help propel Southington past Maloney 38-14 at Falcon Field. The Blue Knights led by just 17-14 when Beaulieu took an inside screen from quarterback Jacoby Roman on the first snap of the final frame and turned it into a 45-yard, reverse-field excursion to the end zone. Beaulieu's 61-yard breakaway five minutes later, coupled with a 37-yard TD run by senior Nick Andrews, made it a runaway down the stretch as Southington scored 31 unanswered points in all to bounce back from last week's loss to New Britian to improve to 8-1. With Staples losing 28-7 to Fairfield Ludlowe, the Blue Knights now stand No. 1 in the Class LL playoff race. Maloney, meanwhile, fell to No. 10 in Class L at 6-3 despite holding the lead in the second quarter. After spotting Southington a 7-0 advantage courtesy of a Beaulieu 2-yard run, the Spartans shot ahead 14-7 on two long strikes from QB Eli Showerda to Jameir Diaz (42 yards) and Cayden Simonds Gaskin (66). Southington answered with a game-tying 10-yard pass from Jacoby Roman to Andrews, then took a 17-14 lead into halftime when defensive back Andrew Vecchio's interception led to a 45-yard field goal by Jacob Carrier with 0:37 on the clock. Another key sequence came in the third quarter, even though neither team scored. The Spartans held Southington on a fourth-and-2 just inside their own 20 to open the half, then drove inside the Blue Knights' 8. Tyler Tortora dropped Showerda for a 9-yard loss on a bootleg pass on third down and Maloney kicker Eli Osei's 34-yard field goal attempt was off the mark. A few snaps later, on the first play of the fourth quarter, Beaulieu was gone on that inside screen. This story will be updated. Player of the Game Ben Beaulieu: Southington's junior running back scored three touchdowns and also shored up the secondary, breaking up a Maloney pass in the end zone. Quotable "I said to you last week about how we were going to suck every ounce of learning out of that (New Britain) game, and (our players) were committed to that as soon as we started Saturday morning at 8 a.m. in the weight room. They wanted to fix us and we had to fix us ... We had kids step up tonight and that's a program win." - Southington coach Rob Levesque. item.title: Second half costs Castle football in Class 5A regional championship game
item.description: BLOOMINGTON — Talent took over in Bloomington on Friday, November 13. It began as a tight game between Castle and Bloomington South football in the IHSAA Class 5A regional championship. The Knights’ Ben Quach scored the game’s first touchdown following a goal-line stop that held the Panthers to a field goal. It was an impressive catch in the back of the end zone, and the throw from quarterback Sawyer Winsett was put in a spot where only the senior could catch it. More: Southwestern Indiana regional football scores, updates Bloomington South responded with a touchdown from quarterback Duncan Combs on a sneak that would make it 10-7. Then, Castle responded with a drive that featured multiple conversions, eventually leading to a short-yardage rushing touchdown from senior Austin Pritchard. Bloomington South offered another response from another Combs rush into the end zone. It was 17-14 at halftime. But in the second half, outside of a stop on Bloomington South’s opening drive, the Knights simply could not keep up with the No. 3 team in 5A, falling 38-14 to end their season. A tale of two halves The Panthers scored 21 on three-straight possessions in the second half: a passing touchdown to wide receiver Jonathan Winstead, and two receiving touchdowns from wide receiver Mayson Lewis. Castle’s offense could not move the ball down the field as it did in the first half. Each drive was short, rarely getting past its own side of the field. Defensively, Combs and his surrounding cast overwhelmed the Knights in both passing and running the football. While Castle’s season has come to an end, still, Castle coach Doug Hurt is proud of what his group accomplished. It did not always seem likely they would end up here. “This might be one of the biggest turnarounds I’ve ever had,” Hurt said. “We’ve had teams where we got better, but just in terms of the general attitude and effort and love for each other, it’s one of the most remarkable things that I’ve seen. If you would have asked me or the public five weeks ago if Castle would be down three against Bloomington South at half of the regional final game, I don’t think many people would have believed.” Hurt has a close relationship with Bloomington South coach Gabe Johnson. The two played college football together at Indiana State. Johnson praised Castle’s attitude and effort in a conversation with Hurt after the game. item.title: Mets Battle Phillies For Japanese Slugger Teruaki Sato
item.description: Sep 20, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; New York Mets center fielder A.J. Ewing (9) reacts during an at bat against the Philadelphia Phillies during the ninth inning at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images The New York Mets are throwing their hat into the ring for one of the most sought-after hitters in baseball. According to Bob Nightengale of USA Today , the team is actively pursuing Teruaki Sato, a Japanese slugger who just won a Triple Crown in his home league. The pursuit of Teruaki Sato signals that the front office is ready to spend big to fill a hole in the outfield. The Mets are not alone in this pursuit, but the fact that they are in the mix shows serious intent. A Market With No Quiet Corners Philadelphia, the New York Yankees, and the San Diego Padres are also chasing Sato . USA Today Sports’ MLB insider Bob Nightengale highlighted the fierce rivalry around the player. He says, “Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato is the position player everyone wants,” and that his market is already sizable. The Mets face stiff competition from teams with deeper pockets and more immediate needs. Yet, the presence of the Mets on the list suggests they view Sato as a key piece for the future. Sato turns 28 years old in March, bringing youth to a roster that has leaned on older veterans. His stats from last season are hard to ignore. He posted a .306 batting average with 39 home runs and 106 RBI in the NPB. These numbers prove he can handle power pitching, even if he comes from a different league. The Mets need that kind of production if they want to challenge for a title again. Defensive Fit and Roster Questions While Sato played third base in Japan, scouts believe he will end up in the outfield. This shift matters for the Mets because they have open spots in the outfield but need to sort out their infield. The Phillies have similar questions about Trea Turner and the third-base spot. The Mets can avoid the infield drama by placing Sato in the field where he fits best. This allows them to keep their current infield plans intact while adding a new weapon. Some teams worry about his strikeout rate, but scouts say his approach is better than the raw numbers show. He has legitimate power potential that fits the modern game perfectly. The Mets have shown they are willing to take calculated risks on international talent. Adding a left-handed hitter with this much power would balance the lineup significantly. The New York Mets are now officially part of a crowded field trying to sign Teruaki Sato. Per Sports Illustrated, the Phillies, Yankees, and Padres are also ranked as the top teams interested in the player.

item.title: ‘He called me a…’: Draymond Green explains the real reason why he got a fan ‘thrown out’ vs Rockets
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images There were many talking points from the Golden State Warriors’ defeat to the Houston Rockets, and Draymond Green was involved in one of them. The Warriors were not having a great game, and to make things worse, a fan seemed to annoy Green in the fourth quarter. The 36-year-old yelled back at the supporter and then complained to an official, thus getting them removed from their seat and escorted out. Now, Green has explained what really happened. Draymond Green reveals why he got a fan ‘thrown out’ during Warriors vs Rockets Green has never been one to shy away from a confrontation. The Warriors star is always up for a fight, and when a fan at the Toyota Center had something to say to him, he was going to respond. In his podcast on YouTube, Green revealed that he is always open to heckling and taunting from rival fans, but name-calling is where it crosses the line. That is exactly what happened on Wednesday night, which is why he asked for the supporter to be removed from their seat. Green said: “My exchange with the fan, the fan was thrown out. He called me a b****. We’re just not going for that. “You call me that, and you stand up and start cheering. It’s pretty whack because, quite honestly, you ain’t going to stand on that type of time. You ain’t going to come down there and stand on that type of time. “I hate when fans try to do that. If you come to cheer, come to cheer. If you want to heckle, heckle. The name-calling like that, you ain’t really willing to do what comes with that. “So just be a fan. Heckle, taunt all you want. But the name-calling, that don’t go over too well.” Like many of his teammates, Green did not have a great game against the Rockets, which is perhaps why the comment from the fan irritated him even more. The biggest story of the night, however, was Steph Curry going off injured in the first half. It has been confirmed that he will be out for at least two weeks, which is a big blow. It remains to be seen how the Warriors will fare without him in the coming games. item.title: UConn HC Dan Hurley toasts Huskies culture after win over Ohio State
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images UConn HC Dan Hurley toasts Huskies culture after win over Ohio State appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The UConn Huskies passed their first real test of the season on Friday night, and Dan Hurley credited the program’s culture for carrying his team past Ohio State . No. 4 UConn pulled away in the second half for an 84-68 win over the Buckeyes in Hartford, improving to 4-0. Hurley told TNT Sports’ Andy Katz that his team’s identity showed up when it mattered. “I mean, we’re UConn. You know, like, we’re UConn, we’re dealing with some medical stuff, not just with Nik, but, you know, we just got a culture and a mindset, and I think those guys are good. You know, I liken them a lot to the Texas team that came in here last year at this time, and, you know, they got some great pieces, just take a little bit of time to gel,” Hurley said after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dan Hurley tells @TheAndyKatz @UConnMBB 's culture and mindset is what pushed them ahead against Ohio State 🔥 pic.twitter.com/tlwJwrnD9U — TNT Sports U.S. (@TNTSportsUS) November 14, 2026 The Huskies are already playing without forward Nik Khamenia, who is expected to miss several weeks with a foot injury suffered against Wagner . UConn led by double digits early, but the Buckeyes closed the first half on a 13-1 run and trailed just 42-40 at the break. Ohio State then grabbed its first lead early in the second half on a Justin Pippen 3-pointer. That is when Braylon Mullins took over . With UConn down two, Mullins scored five straight points, and Jayden Ross followed with a 3-pointer with 13:57 left. The Huskies never trailed again, outscoring the Buckeyes 42-28 in the second half. Mullins finished with a team-high 22 points and five triples before hobbling off with 6:07 remaining. Na’jai Hines added 20 points on 7-of-8 shooting, scoring 17 of them after halftime. “Well, that’s how you make up for the [Khamenia] loss. You know, we got to get more from our bigs,” Hurley said. He also wants more from his guards and his defense. “We got to have our backcourt show up and play like the best backcourt in the country, and, you know, we got to turn it up at the defensive end like we did the last 12 to 15 minutes,” he added. UConn will face a much tougher test on Wednesday when it visits No. 12 Arizona. item.title: ‘The World’s Strongest Dad’ – Keito Yamakita Heads Into World Title Fight With A New Reason To Win
item.description: Life rarely delivers a man’s two greatest desires in the exact same breath, but for Keito “Pocket Monk” Yamakita , destiny is converging on a single week. The surging Japanese martial artist is currently staring down two massive, life-altering countdowns. One leads directly to a career-defining World Title fight, while the other ticks toward the arrival of his precious firstborn child. That incredible convergence culminates at ONE SAMURAI 5 on Wednesday, November 18, when he officially challenges reigning ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion Joshua “The Passion” Pacio at EBARA WAVE Arena Ota in Tokyo. View this post on Instagram While martial arts has entirely defined Yamakita’s existence since his earliest days on the wrestling mats of Inabe in Mie Prefecture, fatherhood represents a profoundly different kind of unknown. With his wife due to give birth the very day after the World Title match, his heart is already tethered to a far greater miracle waiting just outside the Circle. Yet the 30-year-old candidly admits his sense of maturity has not fully caught up with the monumental shift ahead. Even so, he is eagerly looking forward to growing into the role the moment his son is born. The expectant father told onefc.com: “We’d wanted a child for quite a while, so more than anything I felt relieved that it had actually happened. There were worries too. “And the hundreds of days until the birth seemed so long. It felt endless, but before I knew it, it was almost here. So now I’m feeling a little restless and excited.” Photo credit: ONE Championship Fate may have perfectly aligned the dates, but “Pocket Monk” has spent a lifetime grinding toward this athletic peak. An impressive 6-1 promotional record and a brilliant five-fight winning streak delivered Yamakita to the biggest night of his professional career. Lately, though, his quiet moments reach far beyond himself, extending toward the life that follows. He added: “I’ll be a father while still competing, and I’d love my son to see me fight. That will probably be a little further down the road, but I’m really looking forward to him watching my fights.” View this post on Instagram That nervous anticipation sits alongside steady, unwavering support at home. His wife has never demanded he win a gold belt, only that he returns home in one piece. Still, a profound internal shift has altered how he approaches the grueling work ahead, and the reason is rapidly approaching. The Team We athlete continued: “I was chasing championship belts for myself. Even when I became Pancrase champion in Japan, I felt I was doing it for myself. Now I have my son to do it for as well, so that gives me even more motivation. “I went into fights wanting to give one hundred percent of what I had. Now, with my child in the picture, I feel like I can give one hundred and twenty percent—something beyond what I normally have in me.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship The Example Yamakita Wants To Set For a man standing on the precipice

item.title: Florida High captures elusive complete game in playoff rout vs Jackson
item.description: Every year the postseason rolls around, the saying goes, “win and advance.” No. 4 seed Florida State University School (9-2) did just that on Friday, beating the visiting No. 5 Andrew Jackson High School (7-4) of Jacksonville 42-6 in the FHSAA Class 2A regional quarterfinals at Mike Hickman Stadium. “I’ve seen this for this group and been excited to try to put it all together,” Florida High head coach Jarrod Hickman told the Tallahassee Democrat. “Which is what we needed to do and have to do this time of the year.” Hickman added that he wanted his team to get off to a “fast start,” something that eluded the Seminoles in their two losses this season. Most recently, in a 31-27 shortfall to James S. Rickards in the Oct. 29 regular season finale. “We pushed through adversity,” said quarterback Jayme Miller . “It was hard, but we knew what we had to do.” If one looked down, by the second quarter the Florida High Seminoles were already up 28-0 on the Jackson Tigers. Miller, a junior, tossed four touchdowns on the night. Two went to four-star wide receiver Ar’Tavian ‘Bubba’ Brown . Running back Brisyn Brown and receiver Messiah Anariva caught the others. On the ground, running back Mike Jones reached the end zone, and Brisyn Brown got him one too. Friday was the fifth time the Seminoles cracked 40 points. They average 34.4 points per game. “Lighting up the scoreboard is a big part of the game,” Miller explained. “You just got to go shot for shot. We’re playing good football, but it could be better. There are some things we got to capitalize on.” Florida High also stonewalled the Andrew Jackson Tiger offense that entered Friday averaging 26.9 points per game. Defensive back Gavin Brown notched a fumble recovery at the expense of Jackson quarterback Hans Price. Special teams also forced some turnovers. The lone score for the Tigers was a touchdown pass from Price to Malkiel Pierce. Next for Florida High is a trip to Jacksonville to face the No. 1 seed and Florida high school football powerhouse Bolles School Bulldogs (8-2) in the regional semifinals. They eliminated Freeport 49-7 on Friday. “The test is going to continue to get more challenging,” Hickman said. “And you have to be even that much sharper on the road.” It’s a rematch from the 2025 playoffs, when the Bulldogs defeated the Seminoles 51-27 in last year’s semis. item.title: Caleb Holt’s breakout game leads Arizona men’s basketball past Auburn
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 13: Motiejus Krivas #13 of the Arizona Wildcats defends as Adam Olsen #24 of the Auburn Tigers inbounds the ball during the second half of an NCAA basketball game at Neville Arena on November 13, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Power conference teams, take note: tread lightly when considering scheduling a home-and-home with Arizona. For the second year in a row the Wildcats ended a lengthy home win streak against non-league foes, beating Auburn 80-69 on Friday night. The Tigers had won 71 consecutive nonconference game at Neville Arena, a streak that went back to 2016. Caleb Holt , back in his home state, had a breakout performance with 24 points, nine rebounds and five steals while Ivan Kharchenkov went for 19 points and 8 rebounds and Motiejus Krivas had 16 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. Holt was 4 of 6 from 3-point range after missing 10 of 11 triples in Arizona’s first three games. The Wildcats (3-1) turned it over 12 times, twice as many as in Tuesday’s win over an NAU team that almost upset Kentucky on the road Friday night, and had 12 shots blocked (six by Auburn center Narcisse Ngoy ) but still shot 44.4 percent overall including 50 percent in the second half. Auburn (2-1) shot 34.8 percent, and while it made 11 3s it took 31 and was just 12 of 35 from inside the arc. Junior guard Tahad Pettiford , who came in averaging 22.5 points per game, had nine on 4-of-14 shooting. Arizona outrebounded the Tigers by 12 and finished up 16 in points in the paint despite all the blocked shots. Coach Tommy Lloyd made a lineup change, with JJ Mandaquit replacing Bryce James . The Washington transfer had six points (all on free throws) in 31 minutes while James did not play, nor did backup center Ugnius Jarusevicius. The UA bench logged only 27 minutes with four points, two each from Maksim Brnovic and Evan Otten . Arizona led 36-32 at halftime despite having nine shots blocked and turning it over eight times. The first shot of the 2nd half was swatted as well but the Wildcats still opened on 10-0 run to lead by 14 less than three minutes in. But like in the 1 st half when the UA would get a little separation, Auburn quickly scored on consecutive possessions to get back in it. A 10-2 run got the Tigers within 48-42. The Wildcats were up 51-44 when Krivas picked up his third foul with 13:02 left, and in his absence Auburn went on a 9-2 run to tie it on an Owen Freeman hook shot. Krivas came back in with 9:38 remaining and immediately drew Ngoy’s fourth foul, but he missed the front end of a 1-and-1. Auburn then took its first lead since 18-16 on a Freeman free throw and a 54-53 advantage before Holt got a steal and dunk to put the Wildcats back in front. item.title: Draymond Green Shoves Victor Wembanyama In The Back; ‘Unnecessary’ Flagrant Foul Faces Criticism
item.description: SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 13: Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors plays defense on Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 13, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) The Warriors’ frustrations seemingly boiled over tonight in the second quarter as Draymond Green pushed Victor Wembanyama in the back on a questionable play while tracking back on defense. The veteran was instantly assessed a flagrant foul one for unnecessarily pushing the Spurs’ big man. This sequence came soon after the Warriors’ 0-18 start against the Spurs tonight, which dug them into a major hole they needed to climb out of. And it was right after a play where Victor Wembanyama dunked over Draymond Green. Draymond Green TACKLED Wemby after Wemby dunked on him 💀 — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 14, 2026 NBA fans saw this incident and flooded social media with the Warriors veteran’s criticism. “I like Draymond, but this s–t is dirty. item.title: Ilia Malinin tops Saatva Skate America short program in season debut
item.description: EVERETT, Washington — Ilia Malinin showed a little rust in his first competitive skate since March, but it was still enough to take the lead at Saatva Skate America. Malinin landed a quadruple flip and triple Axel, but then under-rotated a quad Lutz and tacked a double toe onto it rather than a triple toe. He scored 96.74 points, the world's sixth-best short program score through four of six Grand Prix regular season events. He takes a 5.45-point lead over Sota Yamamoto of Japan going into Saturday's free skate (9:30 p.m. ET, Peacock and NBCSN). Skate America continues Saturday starting at 5 p.m. ET with the rhythm dance and women's short program before the men's free skate and pairs' free skate, all live on Peacock . SKATE AMERICA: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Malinin had his 14-event win streak dating to 2023 snapped at the Milan Cortina Olympics, where he went from first after the short program to eighth overall after a disastrous 15th-place free skate. He rebounded to win a third consecutive world title to finish his season in March. Malinin eschewed competing in a lower-level event in September, like he has in past years, to make his season debut on the top-level Grand Prix Series. If all goes to plan, he'll compete three times over the next month. After Skate America, he's slated for NHK Trophy two weeks from now. There, he'll hope to qualify for December's Grand Prix Final, an event he won each of the last three seasons. item.title: Vero Beach blanks Fort Pierce Central, advances to regional semifinals
item.description: VERO BEACH — The Vero Beach High School football team extended a number of streaks with its latest victory. But given how close his team’s last two games were against Fort Pierce Central, longtime Vero Beach coach Lenny Jankowski walked off the field less concerned about a string of wins and more focused on being 1-0 in its most recent game. “Each game is independent of the other. But we knew we were in for it tonight,” Jankowski said. “(The Cobras) are a very well-coached team with some really good players. And obviously, we’re familiar with each other being in the same district. We were really just concerned with tonight and pleased with the outcome.” Vero Beach struck first with a surge late in the first half, tacked on a pair of second-half scores and never looked back en route to a 24-0 victory over Fort Pierce Central in a Region 2-6A quarterfinal Friday, Nov. 13, at Billy Livings Field at the Citrus Bowl. Vero Beach collected its eighth consecutive victory this season. The team also extended both its winning streak against the Cobras and its regional quarterfinal winning streak to 14 games. “It’s a big win and a lot of good things happened,” Jankowski said. Latravious Woods finished with two touchdown receptions, the first of which broke the ice in what was a scoreless first half to that point. The junior wide receiver got free on a corner route and hauled in a pass from Makai White for a 58-yard touchdown with 1 minute, 39 seconds remaining in the second quarter. After forcing a punt on the next Central possession, Vero Beach marched 59 yards in a matter of seconds. Synder Arbelaez capped the drive with a 26-yard field goal to put the home team ahead 10-0 at halftime. Vero Beach added to its lead late in the third quarter. Following an interception by Jeromie King, White connected with Sebastian Cabrera on a 57-yard reception down the sideline to put Vero Beach on the doorstep. Three plays later, Woods notched his second touchdown of the night after taking a wide receiver screen 10 yards into the end zone. On the previous play, Woods showed some frustration after White did not look his way. But the ball found the junior on the next snap, and he did what he does best after the catch. “Playing with Makai is great. I love playing with him,” Woods said. “He’s young, so I know I got to stay on him and keep his preparation right. I’m happy to see him grow and he’s been growing the whole season.” Woods finished with four receptions for 104 yards and four carries for 17 yards. White completed 11 of 19 passes for 214 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. With Vero Beach in command, Marc Johns put a bow on the victory in the fourth quarter. item.title: New Canaan football makes late goal-line stand to hold off Wilton in Week 10 thriller
item.description: Jack Crowell accounted for both touchdowns in New Canaan's 16-12 win over Wilton on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Wilton High. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) WILTON - The New Canaan High football team played yet another nail-biter on Friday night, this time against Wilton at Tom Fujitani Field. This time, the Rams finished off a 16-12 victory over the Warriors, but it came down to one final defensive stand at their own goal line. New Canaan improved to 7-2 while Wilton fell to 4-5. Wilton senior Liam Smith came up with an interception of New Canaan quarterback Maddox Hoffman at the Rams' 24-yard line with 3:41 left in the game. The Warriors pushed the ball to the 10, where they had it on second-and-9 with two minutes remaining. New Canaan's defense stopped Wilton quarterback Connor Harlacher on a draw for no gain, then an incomplete pass from Harlacher brought up fourth-and-9 from the 10 with 1:13 remaining. The Warriors called for a trick play, a lineman-eligible pass from Harlacher to senior Krystian Babinski, but the Rams sniffed it out after just a 2-yard gain to squelch the home team's last gasp. As he has done time and again, New Canaan senior captain Jack Crowell came up big for his team. The Rams trailed 6-0 at halftime, but Crowell took a direct snap for a 53-yard touchdown 1:29 into the third quarter. Neel Arora's extra point put New Canaan ahead 7-6. Wilton senior captain Nicholas Mercado was in the right place at the right time when Maddox, who was in the grasp of a sack, tried to get rid of the ball. It went right to Mercado, who took it 75 yards for a touchdown and a 12-7 Warrior lead late in the third quarter. After New Canaan took advantage of a bad Wilton snap and stopped Denny Dustin in the end zone for a safety that cut Wilton's lead to 12-9 15 seconds into the fourth quarter, the Rams got good field position. New Canaan drove to the Wilton 4, where it faced a fourth-and-3. Crowell, who had run the ball on direct snaps on the previous two plays, took another run toward the right side. He pulled up short, jumped in the air and threw a pass to junior Luke Williams for a 4-yard touchdown and the lead. Arora's extra point made it 16-12 in favor of the Rams with 7:44 left in the game. Wilton punted on its next possession to pin New Canaan deep with 4:38 to play. The Rams ran the ball twice, then Hoffman rolled to his right on third down and threw toward his team's sideline. Smith caught the ball and got both feet in bounds to preserve the pick. On a third-and-9 from the New Canaan 23, Harlacher hit Dustin for a 12-yard gain and a first down at the 11 with 2:53 to play. The Warriors, who had upended Greenwich the week before, were within range of pulling off another huge win. New Canaan's defense stepped up when it had to, however, and preserved the victory. item.title: Five takeaways from UVA basketball’s 87-83 comeback win at Maryland
item.description: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 13: Sam Lewis #5 of the Virginia Cavaliers drives to the basket in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at Xfinity Center on November 13, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Three days after a 34-point rout of Bucknell, No. 6 Virginia went on the road for the first time this season, a Friday night trip to College Park for the second game of a four-game series with Maryland. It was the Cavaliers’ third game in six days and their fifth in 11. Maryland, 1-1 in Buzz Williams’ second season, had not played since an 86-74 loss to Georgetown last Saturday. DraftKings opened Virginia as a 6.5-point favorite, with the line moving to 5.5 by tip. For 20 minutes, almost nothing went right. Virginia turned the ball over eight times, sent Maryland to the free-throw line a whopping 24 times and did not make a three until late in the half. Feeding off a loud, near-capacity crowd of 16,908 at the Xfinity Center, the Terrapins led 47-36 at the break. However, Virginia flipped a switch, and the second half belonged to the ‘Hoos. The Cavaliers shot 20-of-26 from the field, outscored Maryland 51-36 and took their first lead since early in the first half on a Chance Mallory step-back three. Virginia led for only 20 percent of the game, but it took the lead when it mattered most. The Cavaliers move to 5-0, Maryland falls to 1-2, and Virginia has now won 10 of the last 11 meetings against the Terrapins. View this post on Instagram Here are my five takeaways. Down 11 on the road, Virginia showed the grit of a top-10 team This was a tale of two halves for Virginia, and the biggest difference was composure. In the first half, Virginia looked rattled. It started 5-of-17 from the field, missed layups, threw the ball away in the half court and picked up 13 fouls. It seemed like on practically every possession Virginia was sending Maryland to the line, where the Terrapins made 19 of 24 free throws before halftime. The exclamation point was a three to close the half that put Maryland up 11 and sent the crowd into a frenzy. In the second half, Virginia slowed down and went to work. Maryland had no answer for its pick-and-roll offense in the half court.
